# Results — Study 774 (Nintendo-Direct)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**"Buy the hype into a Nintendo Direct"**: does NTDOY rally into the broadcast and/or fade
after? Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint
`a7162a8938fd` (NTDOY + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `NTDOY` (Nintendo ADR) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 3,643 rows, 2012-01-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 25 flagship general/E3 Nintendo Directs 2013→2025, real air dates from Wikipedia / Nintendo Life (2020 absent — no general Direct that year) |
| Events resolvable | all **25** of 25 Directs have NTDOY+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (NTDOY − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; fade = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Look-ahead caveat, named:** a Nintendo Direct is usually announced only **~1-3 days
ahead**, not 7-10 days like an Apple press invite. So a literal "buy 10 sessions before"
rule is **not** genuinely calendar-known — you had to know the exact date to place the
trade. We measure the run-up because it is the folklore, and count the look-ahead against
tradability. **Microstructure caveat:** NTDOY is a thin OTC ADR whose US close can lag the
Tokyo (7974.T) tape, so a US-close-to-US-close AR around a Japan-timed broadcast is partly a
stale-price artefact.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the Direct (NTDOY − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 25 | −1.474% | −1.552 | 10/25 = 40.0% [23.4%, 59.3%] |
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 25 | −1.203% | −0.688 | 12/25 = 48.0% [30.0%, 66.5%] |

The bullish folklore is **not there**: NTDOY does not rally into a Direct. If anything the
sign is *negative* (−1.47% over the last two weeks), but the effect is **not significant**
(*t* = −1.55, |*t*| < 2) and the hit rate is a coin-flip. It is a mild lean, indistinguishable
from noise, not a "sell the run-up" edge.

## The fade — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the Direct

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week fade (k=10) | 25 | +0.925% | +0.774 | 13/25 = 52.0% [33.5%, 70.0%] |
| 1-month fade (k=21) | 25 | −0.096% | −0.053 | 13/25 = 52.0% [33.5%, 70.0%] |

The "sell the news" half is a **clean zero**: post-Direct NTDOY is statistically
indistinguishable from SPY (both cuts |*t*| < 0.8). There is no reliable fade to short, and
no reliable pop to ride.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | −1.474% | −0.028% (1.507%) | 0.844 |
| 2-week fade | left | +0.925% | −0.028% (1.507%) | 0.774 |

The 2-week run-up (right-tail p = 0.844 ⇒ ~16% of random 2-week windows were this negative)
is **not** in the tail of the luck cloud — the pre-Direct dip is ordinary NTDOY tracking
noise, not a special event effect. The fade sits well inside the cloud too (p = 0.77).

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week run-up *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−1.552**; across all 25 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−1.829, −1.140]** — so no single Direct drives the (already insignificant) lean, but it
never gets anywhere near |*t*| ≥ 2 either.

## Tradability — net of costs

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | −1.474% (*t* −1.55) | −1.574% (*t* −1.66) | −1.674% (*t* −1.76) |
| 2-week fade | +0.925% (*t* +0.77) | +0.825% (*t* +0.69) | +0.725% (*t* +0.61) |

Even before costs there is no significant edge; costs only make the (untradeable) short of a
negative window look mildly larger. On top of that: the entry date is **not truly known**
2 weeks out (Directs announced ~1-3 days ahead), NTDOY is a **thin OTC ADR** with wide
spreads and stale-price risk, and this is a 4-window multiple-testing search. Nothing to bank.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = −0.25 (sd 1.06); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds —
  the small-sample false-positive rate at n = 25 events with a 10-day AR is modest (~10%),
  so the detector is honest on the null.
- **Planted run-up +1.0% (seed 778):** mean AR +1.66%, *t* = **+1.44**.
- **Planted run-up +2.0% (seed 778):** mean AR +2.66%, *t* = **+2.31** — a real bump is
  recovered monotonically. The machinery works; the real tape simply has no bump to find.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | Neither half of the folklore survives. The "rally into the Direct" is absent (2-week run-up −1.47%, but *t* = −1.55, |*t*| < 2, placebo right-tail p = 0.84 ⇒ ordinary noise, hit rate 40%); the "sell the news" fade is a clean zero (|*t*| < 0.8). Nothing reaches significance, nothing sits in a placebo tail, and the synthetic null shows the detector would have caught a real bump. Indistinguishable from noise. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank: no significant edge gross or net, the exact entry date isn't known 2 weeks out (Directs announced ~1-3 days ahead), and NTDOY is a thin OTC ADR with wide spreads and stale-price risk. |

**In one sentence:** "Buy the hype into a Nintendo Direct" is a bust — NTDOY neither reliably
rallies into the broadcast (a mild, insignificant dip if anything) nor fades after (a clean
zero), and any faint lean drowns in an illiquid ADR's tracking noise.
